materialBlockers: Canonical documents used unqualified Step 1 wording even though the approved claim was narrower.
Acceptance said exact source while the self-contained fallback intentionally contained deployed runtime source and verification inputs rather than all 79 repository files.
The snapshot verifier did not enforce its required manifest binding set, so a weakened snapshot manifest could bypass it.
Committed CI evidence was not API-bound to its run ID, head SHA, conclusion, job, and artifact digest.
Acceptance, verifier, and workflow were not frozen together before final review, and review records could be self-declared without a strict final-only diff.
Canonical status validation checked only the presence of a vocabulary word instead of exact Step 1A and later-step states.
Fresh Preview evidence stored observed hashes but not raw injected HTML and response headers needed to recalculate the only normalized paths.
The local and remote review histories had identical trees but different commit lineages, while the successful CI belonged only to the remote lineage.

failureRecord.mistakenCompletion: A successful clean-room CI run was nearly treated as sufficient even though the completion claim and its validator still had semantic and provenance bypasses.
failureRecord.expectationGap: A human expects the saved checkpoint claim, the evidence, and the automated judge to describe the same recoverable object and resist a convenient self-authored PASS.
failureRecord.rootCause: The first reconstruction strengthened runtime testing faster than it strengthened claim semantics and evidence provenance.
failureRecord.reuse: Keep the exact runtime snapshot, 17-path manifest, successful CI run, raw local evidence, Vercel rebuild, and honest legacy limitations.
failureRecord.discardOrRebuild: Replace the Acceptance and final validator contract, narrow the scope name everywhere, bind CI through GitHub's API, capture raw Preview HTML, and continue only from remote commit lineage 5792be4.

nextRoundHypothesis: A third-round Acceptance that names only the deployed browser runtime source and deployment inputs, freezes its judge before final review, and API-binds CI can support a defensible Step 1A PASS without claiming player-save or physical-device capabilities.
